There were 63 participants, of whom 33 received KRG and 30 received a placebo. The mtDNA copy number (KRG group: 1.58 ± 2.05, placebo group: 0.28 ± 2.36, p = 0.023) and TAS (KRG group: 0.11 ± 0.25 mmol/L, placebo group: −0.04 ± 0.16 mmol/L, p = 0.011) increased and the fatigue severity scale (KRG group: −7 ± 12, placebo group: −1 ± 11, p = 0.033) decreased significantly more in the KRG group than the placebo group. KRG significantly increased the mtDNA copy number, total antioxidant status, and improved symptoms of fatigue in postmenopausal women.Keywords: Korean red ginseng, antioxidant activity, biological aging, fatigue, postmenopausal women

2.1. Study Design and Participants

P
This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial. Participants were examined at the Severance Health Check-up, Severance Hospital, Yonsei University Health System, in Seoul, Korea, between August 2019 and March 2021. This study’s protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Gangnam Severance Hospital (IRB no.: 3-2019-0089) and registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS, KCT0006506). This study was performed in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

P
Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years who could communicate in Korean naturally and who were not participating in any other interventional studies. Additionally, participants had to have no physical restrictions on movement. Those who were excluded were current smokers; those who consumed more than 3 standard alcoholic drinks more than two days per week; who had uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥ 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) ≥ 100 mmHg; who had uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, defined as having fasting plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL; who had been diagnosed with liver disease and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels more than three times the upper limit; who had been diagnosed with kidney, cardiovascular, or cerebral vascular disease; who had any form of cancer or were undergoing cancer treatment; or who were taking other health supplements or female hormones. Written informed consent was obtained from all patients before participation.

P
A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

2.5.1. Total Antioxidant Status

P
TAS was measured using a TBA c8000 automated colorimeter (Toshiba Medical system Ltd., Tokyo, Japan). The antioxidative molecules in the sample reduce dark blue-green-colored 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzo-thiazoline-6-sulfonate) radicals into a colorless form according to antioxidant concentrations and capacities. The change in absorbance at 660 nm is related to the total amount of antioxidants in the sample. The TAS assay was calibrated with Trolox equivalent, a stable, standard antioxidant solution and a vitamin E analog [12].

TITLE
2.5.3. Fatigue Severity Scale

P
The FSS is a popular tool for measuring fatigue symptoms [13]. It has been validated for various diseases, such as multiple sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosis, Parkinson’s disease, and stroke [14,15,16]. It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points. Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

4. Discussion

P
This study comprised a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the effect of KRG consumption on biological aging, antioxidant capacity, and fatigue symptoms in postmenopausal women. We found that taking 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks increased mtDNA copy number and TAS and reduced fatigue symptoms more than the placebo. Our findings are consistent with those of previous studies on the effectiveness of KRG.

P
First, in this study, KRG was shown to increase the mtDNA copy number more than the placebo. A previous study showed that KRG improved exercise performance, increased the ATP production capacity of muscle cells, and stimulated myoblast differentiation in mice [17]. An animal study showed that the mtDNA copy number and messenger RNA expression levels of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors increased more in those with diabetes who took KRG than those who took a placebo [18]. A clinical trial showed that the mtDNA copy number for men with metabolic syndromes increased when they consumed 3 g/day of KRG and the mean change in their mtDNA copy number was significantly higher than that of the group who consumed a placebo [19].

Another randomized, placebo-controlled study did not show that KRG consumption resulted in a significant decrease in fatigue symptoms for the full sample, but a subgroup analysis showed that it did for people over 50 years old with moderate fatigue symptoms [33]. In this study, the KRG could reduce fatigue symptoms in postmenopausal women as confirmed with statical significance after the intervention.

On the other hand, the mean LDL cholesterol levels in the KRG group decreased from 136 to 127 mg/dL, but they did not decrease in the placebo group. However, this decrease was not statistically significant (p = 0.067). A previous study showed that administering 6 g/day of P. ginseng extract for 8 weeks decreased LDL cholesterol in males [34]. Another clinical study with hyperlipidemic patients reported that LDL cholesterol decreased significantly in the red ginseng (2 g/day) and placebo group, but there was no significant difference between the two groups [35]. The subjects of that study were young, male, and hyperlipidemic, while this study was conducted on postmenopausal women. Therefore, this difference seems to indicate a dissimilarity in the study results. However, even though the baseline LDL cholesterol level was in the normal range, it showed a tendency to decrease after the intervention in postmenopausal women. This study is the first randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to investigate the comprehensive efficacy of KRG administration on biological aging, antioxidant activity, and clinical symptoms in Korean postmenopausal women. However, this study also has some limitations. The first limitation is that the KRG group was administered 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks. Previous clinical studies that evaluated changes in mtDNA copy number, antioxidant indicators, and clinical symptoms varied the dose of KRG from 1 to 6 g/day and the duration of administration from 2 to 12 weeks. These ranges indicate that the dose and duration of KRG administration are not strongly agreed upon, so use of higher doses or longer administration durations in this study may have produced different outcomes, including LDL cholesterol. However, a daily dose of 2 g of KRG is generally available as a healthy functional supplement in the market. Accordingly, in this study, we selected 2 g per day, the dosage for safety KRG intake as a general health functional food. Therefore, determining the optimal dose and duration for KRG intervention should be further investigated in the future. The second limitation is that, although we told the participants to keep their usual lifestyle during the clinical trial, we could not strictly control each individual’s behaviors, which could affect biological aging, antioxidant capacity, and clinical symptoms. The third limitation is that the participants were all Korean postmenopausal women, so the results may not be broadly generalizable to other populations, such as men, premenopausal women, and different ethnicities.

TITLE
5. Conclusions

P
This study examined the effects of KRG consumption on the primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms, in Korean postmenopausal women. The results showed that administering 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks increased the mtDNA copy number, increased antioxidant activity, and reduced fatigue symptoms more than the placebo.

TITLE
2.2. Randomization

P
Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily. Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code. These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute, Inc., Cary, NC, USA). Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

TITLE
2.3. Korean Red Ginseng and Placebo Supplements

P
Participants in the KRG group received 2 g of KRG tablet per day. The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd. The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet). The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets. The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

TITLE

4. Discussion

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Population/design/registration
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Study examination dates
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: between August 2019 and March 2021

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Inclusion and exclusion population
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Randomized allocation denominator
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Active attrition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: 4 participants from the KRG group were excluded

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Placebo attrition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Six participants were excluded from the placebo group

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Dose route frequency
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Sequence allocation wording
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Allocation software
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Blinding
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Composition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Extract preparation
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Placebo matrix
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Intervention supplier
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: FSS item format
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: FSS printed summed range
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical rationale
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: We analyzed the data based on the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem because each group had at least 30 participants.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical between contrast
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The mean differences in changes between the groups were compared using independent two-sample t-tests.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical threshold
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: All statistical tests were two-sided and p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Blood extraction
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: All DNA samples were extracted from ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-treated blood.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: mtDNA formula
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Ct18S–CtND5, where the mean amount of mtDNA = 2−ΔCt

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Outcome hierarchy
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Funding
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: This study was supported by a 2018 research grant from the Korean Society of Ginseng (GS 305-354).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Conflict declaration
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Not applicable.

flags.source_bound_issue: KRG tablet dehydrated from extract; no full botanical extraction recipe, extraction solvent, specific manufacturer/brand/lot or independent purity certificate provided.
flags.consequence: Preparation-specific evidence; generic retail KRG, raw ginseng and isolates equivalence UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The eight listed concentrations describe a mixture. Actual adherence, exposure/PK, and isolated ingredient contributions were not measured.
flags.consequence: Empty ingredient aliases; conditional nominal doses are not efficacy or exposure evidence.

flags.source_bound_issue: Cornstarch/cellulose and same flavor described; quantities, visual/texture matching and blinding success assessment not reported.
flags.consequence: Reported double blinding retained; verified masking success UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Source says SAS-generated codes and sequential alternating assignment by code; method of sequence generation, allocation concealment and implementation details insufficient to reconstruct.
flags.consequence: Retain source RCT claim with unclear allocation wording; neither assured concealment nor definite nonrandom assignment inferred.

flags.source_bound_issue: The main article names SAS 9.4 for allocation, whereas the registry names SAS 9.2.
flags.consequence: Printed conflict retained; original actual software/version UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The article reports 73 randomized (37/36) and 63 completed (33/30). Active losses: two unknown reasons in text versus two lost contact in the native flowchart, one surgery admission, one multivitamin use. Placebo losses: one abdominal pain, two constipation, one multivitamin use, two other-ginseng use.
flags.consequence: Completer analysis rather than claimed ITT; reasons do not establish causality.

flags.source_bound_issue: Endpoint-specific n, imputation, missing-not-at-random sensitivity and ITT estimates not provided.
flags.consequence: Selection by completion may bias estimates; do not assume complete63 for every molecular assay.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry target is 80 (40 per arm); its Final Enrollment Number field is 63, whereas the article reports 73 randomized and 63 analyzed completers.
flags.consequence: Preserve labels; actual target enrollment is not analyzed denominator, registry63 not proof only63 randomized.

flags.source_bound_issue: CRIS first submission is 2021-08-12 and registration is 2021-08-26, after study completion on 2021-03-20; WHO explicitly marks Prospective Registration No.
flags.consequence: Current registration cannot establish outcome prespecification before recruitment or analysis.

flags.source_bound_issue: Article examination dates are August 2019–March 2021. Registry first enrollment is 2019-10-04, primary completion 2020-06-26, study completion 2021-03-20.
flags.consequence: Different date meanings retained; do not infer exact participant overlap or undocumented amendment.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry primary outcomes include DNA telomere length and total oxidative status in addition to mtDNA/TAS. The extra two primary outcomes are not reported in this main article.
flags.consequence: Reporting-completeness concern; no outcome-failure or deliberate selectivity inference.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry planned assessments include BUN, creatinine, urine analysis, body composition, and menopause rating scale in the lay summary. The main reports FSS and limited metabolic labs; these extra outcomes are not reported.
flags.consequence: Missing outcome reporting remains UNKNOWN, not null renal/muscle/menopause results.

flags.source_bound_issue: The protocol field is labeled flow chart.pdf. The results field is labeled Table_Results.pdf, but both WHO-linked and direct endpoints delivered identical two-page flowchart bytes (SHA2564622991b...). No genuine methods protocol, SAP or results-table attachment was obtained.
flags.consequence: One complete flow attachment read; zero complete protocol/SAP/results-table attachment credit.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is explicitly secondary; biomarkers are primary. No prospectively bound fatigue threshold or primary strength endpoint is available.
flags.consequence: Narrow subjective-fatigue qualification only; not definitive primary clinical function efficacy.

flags.source_bound_issue: Tests use unadjusted two-sided P<.05 across metabolic variables, mtDNA change/fold, TAS and FSS. No multiplicity correction, prespecified SAP or confirmatory hierarchy is provided.
flags.consequence: Reported P retained; falsepositive/selectivity uncertainty, not automatic corrected significant result.

flags.source_bound_issue: The article cites the CLT/law of large numbers with at least 30 participants per group, but gives no effect-based power/sample-size calculation or comparative CIs.
flags.consequence: Nonsignificance not equivalence; distribution assumptions and clinical precision UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Baseline leukocytes are 4890±931 versus 5553±1361 (P=.027), and total cholesterol 230±31 versus 210±41 (P=.034). No baseline-adjusted outcome model is reported.
flags.consequence: Potential confounding/precision and blood-cell composition concern; no proven cause of outcome.

flags.source_bound_issue: Usual lifestyle was encouraged, but authors acknowledge it was not strictly controlled. Baseline physical activity is 17/33 versus 10/30 (P=.145).
flags.consequence: No randomized exercise effect; nonsignificant baseline differences do not prove equality.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS has nine items scored 1–7; the printed summed range is 7–63. The conditional arithmetic minimum is 9 if all nine items score 1.
flags.consequence: Retain7–63literal; conditional arithmetic audit not correction of questionnaire scoring.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is self-report. The discussion calls fatigue objectively evaluated using a validated questionnaire, but no objective strength or task test was performed.
flags.consequence: Self-report instrument, not force/performance/strength gain.

flags.source_bound_issue: Exact Korean version, validation in this population, recall window, missing-item rule, MCID and responder threshold are not supplied. No fatigue severity entry criterion is stated.
flags.consequence: Clinical importance and applicability to symptomatic chronic fatigue UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Reported visits are baseline and eight weeks only. Long-term follow-up and post-withdrawal durability are not reported.
flags.consequence: Do not extrapolate long-term efficacy/safety.

flags.source_bound_issue: Relative blood mtDNA qPCR and TAS are proxies. Mitochondrial respiration, ATP, muscle bioenergetics, pathway activation and clinical aging endpoints were not measured.
flags.consequence: No proved aging reversal or muscle mitochondrial rescue.

flags.source_bound_issue: Introduction calls the measure lymphocyte mtDNA; methods describe DNA from EDTA peripheral blood without lymphocyte isolation or subtype adjustment.
flags.consequence: Cell composition influence and exact lymphocyte specificity UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The printed formula defines ΔCt=Ct18S−CtND5 and quantity=2^−ΔCt. Under the usual equal-efficiency ND5/18S normalization this appears to reverse the sign convention.
flags.consequence: Retain printed equation; conditional algebra only, rawCt/calculationverification unavailable.

flags.source_bound_issue: Table1 KRG baseline mtDNA is 4.35±2.54, while Table3/body gives 4.36±2.54.
flags.consequence: Retain both; do not silently normalize rounding.

flags.source_bound_issue: Native Figure2B labels eight-week KRG mtDNA 5.98; Table3/body prints 5.93.
flags.consequence: No plot/table source equivalence assumption; retain5.98and5.93.

flags.source_bound_issue: Table2 KRG gamma-GT means are 17→19 U/L, while reported change is −2±7; arithmetic from those means would give +2.
flags.consequence: Retain printednegativechangeandnullP=.243; conditional arithmetic not data repair.

flags.source_bound_issue: KRG baseline DBP is 73.0±11.6 in Table1 versus 73.3±11.6 in Table2. Placebo baseline SD is 7.9 in Table1 versus 9.6 in Table2. Table2 KRG change is 1.4 despite printed means 74.4−73.3=1.1.
flags.consequence: Printed conflicts/rounded-summary limits retained; no automatic correction.

flags.source_bound_issue: All 12 Table2 comparative P values are at least .05, including LDL .064 and AST .082. No metabolic within-group change is reported as significant.
flags.consequence: Preserve nulls; trends do not become positive efficacy or universal absence.

flags.source_bound_issue: No participant-level association/mediation analysis linking FSS to biomarkers, or pathway experiment, is reported.
flags.consequence: TAS/mtDNA cochanges do not prove fatigue mechanism.

flags.source_bound_issue: Placebo gastrointestinal withdrawals and active surgery/lost-contact cases are described. There is no systematic AE grade/frequency table, causality/severity assessment, or complete serious-event follow-up.
flags.consequence: Formal AE/SAEtotal UNKNOWN, not zero; placeboevents do not prove KRG harmless.

flags.source_bound_issue: Kidney disease was excluded. The registry planned creatinine/BUN, but these results are not reported in the article.
flags.consequence: No renal safety conclusion, no extension to renal disease or general drug interactions.

flags.source_bound_issue: Population is Korean postmenopausal women aged 46–69 without movement restrictions, not an MVA/BUB1B cohort. No objective strength test was reported.
flags.consequence: No population/formulation pooling, sex extrapolation or BUB1B/MVA rescue.

flags.source_bound_issue: The Korean Society of Ginseng funded the study (2018, GS305-354) and supplied tablets. Registry project ID is 2174-2498 and sponsor is Yonsei/Gangnam Severance Hospital. Authors declare no conflicts.
flags.consequence: Funding/supply context preserved; project identity/independent product provenance UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Article data availability is Not applicable; registry IPD sharing is No.
flags.consequence: No rawdata/patient-level reanalysis or exposure confirmation.

flags.source_bound_issue: Current EPMC has no commentCorrectionList and hasSuppl N; XML has no related-article or supplementary-material nodes. Main HTML and Notes return403; browser Notes returns429. Bounded searches retrieved no exact new notice body.
flags.consequence: No current publisher-equivalence or exhaustive no-notice claim; zero notice bodies read.

flags.source_bound_issue: History listing shows one 2021-08-12 row. No separate historical version-detail body was opened.
flags.consequence: No prospective historical plan/amendment equivalence claim.

TITLE
4. Discussion

original_parent_anchor.label: Population/design/registration
original_parent_anchor.literal: This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial.

original_parent_anchor.label: Study examination dates
original_parent_anchor.literal: between August 2019 and March 2021

original_parent_anchor.label: Inclusion and exclusion population
original_parent_anchor.literal: Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years

original_parent_anchor.label: Randomized allocation denominator
original_parent_anchor.literal: A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

original_parent_anchor.label: Active attrition
original_parent_anchor.literal: 4 participants from the KRG group were excluded

original_parent_anchor.label: Placebo attrition
original_parent_anchor.literal: Six participants were excluded from the placebo group

original_parent_anchor.label: Dose route frequency
original_parent_anchor.literal: Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily.

original_parent_anchor.label: Sequence allocation wording
original_parent_anchor.literal: Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code.

original_parent_anchor.label: Allocation software
original_parent_anchor.literal: These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4

original_parent_anchor.label: Blinding
original_parent_anchor.literal: Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

original_parent_anchor.label: Composition
original_parent_anchor.literal: The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd.

original_parent_anchor.label: Extract preparation
original_parent_anchor.literal: The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet).

original_parent_anchor.label: Placebo matrix
original_parent_anchor.literal: The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets.

original_parent_anchor.label: Intervention supplier
original_parent_anchor.literal: The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

original_parent_anchor.label: FSS item format
original_parent_anchor.literal: It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points.

original_parent_anchor.label: FSS printed summed range
original_parent_anchor.literal: Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical rationale
original_parent_anchor.literal: We analyzed the data based on the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem because each group had at least 30 participants.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical between contrast
original_parent_anchor.literal: The mean differences in changes between the groups were compared using independent two-sample t-tests.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical threshold
original_parent_anchor.literal: All statistical tests were two-sided and p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

original_parent_anchor.label: Blood extraction
original_parent_anchor.literal: All DNA samples were extracted from ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-treated blood.

original_parent_anchor.label: mtDNA formula
original_parent_anchor.literal: Ct18S–CtND5, where the mean amount of mtDNA = 2−ΔCt

original_parent_anchor.label: Outcome hierarchy
original_parent_anchor.literal: primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms

original_parent_anchor.label: Funding
original_parent_anchor.literal: This study was supported by a 2018 research grant from the Korean Society of Ginseng (GS 305-354).

original_parent_anchor.label: Conflict declaration
original_parent_anchor.literal: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

original_parent_anchor.literal: Not applicable.

TITLE
4. Discussion

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: KRG tablet dehydrated from extract; no full botanical extraction recipe, extraction solvent, specific manufacturer/brand/lot or independent purity certificate provided.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Preparation-specific evidence; generic retail KRG, raw ginseng and isolates equivalence UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The eight listed concentrations describe a mixture. Actual adherence, exposure/PK, and isolated ingredient contributions were not measured.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Empty ingredient aliases; conditional nominal doses are not efficacy or exposure evidence.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Cornstarch/cellulose and same flavor described; quantities, visual/texture matching and blinding success assessment not reported.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Reported double blinding retained; verified masking success UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Source says SAS-generated codes and sequential alternating assignment by code; method of sequence generation, allocation concealment and implementation details insufficient to reconstruct.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Retain source RCT claim with unclear allocation wording; neither assured concealment nor definite nonrandom assignment inferred.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The main article names SAS 9.4 for allocation, whereas the registry names SAS 9.2.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Printed conflict retained; original actual software/version UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The article reports 73 randomized (37/36) and 63 completed (33/30). Active losses: two unknown reasons in text versus two lost contact in the native flowchart, one surgery admission, one multivitamin use. Placebo losses: one abdominal pain, two constipation, one multivitamin use, two other-ginseng use.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Completer analysis rather than claimed ITT; reasons do not establish causality.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Endpoint-specific n, imputation, missing-not-at-random sensitivity and ITT estimates not provided.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Selection by completion may bias estimates; do not assume complete63 for every molecular assay.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Registry target is 80 (40 per arm); its Final Enrollment Number field is 63, whereas the article reports 73 randomized and 63 analyzed completers.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Preserve labels; actual target enrollment is not analyzed denominator, registry63 not proof only63 randomized.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: CRIS first submission is 2021-08-12 and registration is 2021-08-26, after study completion on 2021-03-20; WHO explicitly marks Prospective Registration No.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Current registration cannot establish outcome prespecification before recruitment or analysis.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Article examination dates are August 2019–March 2021. Registry first enrollment is 2019-10-04, primary completion 2020-06-26, study completion 2021-03-20.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Different date meanings retained; do not infer exact participant overlap or undocumented amendment.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Registry primary outcomes include DNA telomere length and total oxidative status in addition to mtDNA/TAS. The extra two primary outcomes are not reported in this main article.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Reporting-completeness concern; no outcome-failure or deliberate selectivity inference.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Registry planned assessments include BUN, creatinine, urine analysis, body composition, and menopause rating scale in the lay summary. The main reports FSS and limited metabolic labs; these extra outcomes are not reported.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Missing outcome reporting remains UNKNOWN, not null renal/muscle/menopause results.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The protocol field is labeled flow chart.pdf. The results field is labeled Table_Results.pdf, but both WHO-linked and direct endpoints delivered identical two-page flowchart bytes (SHA2564622991b...). No genuine methods protocol, SAP or results-table attachment was obtained.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: One complete flow attachment read; zero complete protocol/SAP/results-table attachment credit.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is explicitly secondary; biomarkers are primary. No prospectively bound fatigue threshold or primary strength endpoint is available.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Narrow subjective-fatigue qualification only; not definitive primary clinical function efficacy.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Tests use unadjusted two-sided P<.05 across metabolic variables, mtDNA change/fold, TAS and FSS. No multiplicity correction, prespecified SAP or confirmatory hierarchy is provided.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Reported P retained; falsepositive/selectivity uncertainty, not automatic corrected significant result.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The article cites the CLT/law of large numbers with at least 30 participants per group, but gives no effect-based power/sample-size calculation or comparative CIs.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Nonsignificance not equivalence; distribution assumptions and clinical precision UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Baseline leukocytes are 4890±931 versus 5553±1361 (P=.027), and total cholesterol 230±31 versus 210±41 (P=.034). No baseline-adjusted outcome model is reported.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Potential confounding/precision and blood-cell composition concern; no proven cause of outcome.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Usual lifestyle was encouraged, but authors acknowledge it was not strictly controlled. Baseline physical activity is 17/33 versus 10/30 (P=.145).
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: No randomized exercise effect; nonsignificant baseline differences do not prove equality.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: FSS has nine items scored 1–7; the printed summed range is 7–63. The conditional arithmetic minimum is 9 if all nine items score 1.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Retain7–63literal; conditional arithmetic audit not correction of questionnaire scoring.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is self-report. The discussion calls fatigue objectively evaluated using a validated questionnaire, but no objective strength or task test was performed.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Self-report instrument, not force/performance/strength gain.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Exact Korean version, validation in this population, recall window, missing-item rule, MCID and responder threshold are not supplied. No fatigue severity entry criterion is stated.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Clinical importance and applicability to symptomatic chronic fatigue UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Reported visits are baseline and eight weeks only. Long-term follow-up and post-withdrawal durability are not reported.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Do not extrapolate long-term efficacy/safety.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Relative blood mtDNA qPCR and TAS are proxies. Mitochondrial respiration, ATP, muscle bioenergetics, pathway activation and clinical aging endpoints were not measured.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: No proved aging reversal or muscle mitochondrial rescue.

observations.literal_anchor:
There were 63 participants, of whom 33 received KRG and 30 received a placebo. The mtDNA copy number (KRG group: 1.58 ± 2.05, placebo group: 0.28 ± 2.36, p = 0.023) and TAS (KRG group: 0.11 ± 0.25 mmol/L, placebo group: −0.04 ± 0.16 mmol/L, p = 0.011) increased and the fatigue severity scale (KRG group: −7 ± 12, placebo group: −1 ± 11, p = 0.033) decreased significantly more in the KRG group than the placebo group. KRG significantly increased the mtDNA copy number, total antioxidant status, and improved symptoms of fatigue in postmenopausal women.Keywords: Korean red ginseng, antioxidant activity, biological aging, fatigue, postmenopausal women

2.1. Study Design and Participants

P
This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial. Participants were examined at the Severance Health Check-up, Severance Hospital, Yonsei University Health System, in Seoul, Korea, between August 2019 and March 2021. This study’s protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Gangnam Severance Hospital (IRB no.: 3-2019-0089) and registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS, KCT0006506). This study was performed in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

P
Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years who could communicate in Korean naturally and who were not participating in any other interventional studies. Additionally, participants had to have no physical restrictions on movement. Those who were excluded were current smokers; those who consumed more than 3 standard alcoholic drinks more than two days per week; who had uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥ 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) ≥ 100 mmHg; who had uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, defined as having fasting plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL; who had been diagnosed with liver disease and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels more than three times the upper limit; who had been diagnosed with kidney, cardiovascular, or cerebral vascular disease; who had any form of cancer or were undergoing cancer treatment; or who were taking other health supplements or female hormones. Written informed consent was obtained from all patients before participation.

P
A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

2.5.1. Total Antioxidant Status

P
TAS was measured using a TBA c8000 automated colorimeter (Toshiba Medical system Ltd., Tokyo, Japan). The antioxidative molecules in the sample reduce dark blue-green-colored 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzo-thiazoline-6-sulfonate) radicals into a colorless form according to antioxidant concentrations and capacities. The change in absorbance at 660 nm is related to the total amount of antioxidants in the sample. The TAS assay was calibrated with Trolox equivalent, a stable, standard antioxidant solution and a vitamin E analog [12].

TITLE
2.5.2. Mitochondria DNA Copy Number

P
All DNA samples were extracted from ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-treated blood. High-quality genomic DNA was extracted from participants’ peripheral blood using a QIAamp DNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The concentration and purity of total DNA were controlled by taking absorbance readings at 260 and 280 nm using a Nanodrop 1000 spectrophotometer (preQLab Biotechnology, Erlangen, Germany). The relative mtDNA copy number was measured by quantitative real-time PCR. Two pairs of primers were designed and used to quantify the mtDNA copy number. TITLE
2.5.3. Fatigue Severity Scale

P
The FSS is a popular tool for measuring fatigue symptoms [13]. It has been validated for various diseases, such as multiple sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosis, Parkinson’s disease, and stroke [14,15,16]. It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points. Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

4. Discussion

P
This study comprised a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the effect of KRG consumption on biological aging, antioxidant capacity, and fatigue symptoms in postmenopausal women. We found that taking 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks increased mtDNA copy number and TAS and reduced fatigue symptoms more than the placebo. Our findings are consistent with those of previous studies on the effectiveness of KRG.

P
First, in this study, KRG was shown to increase the mtDNA copy number more than the placebo. A previous study showed that KRG improved exercise performance, increased the ATP production capacity of muscle cells, and stimulated myoblast differentiation in mice [17]. An animal study showed that the mtDNA copy number and messenger RNA expression levels of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors increased more in those with diabetes who took KRG than those who took a placebo [18]. A clinical trial showed that the mtDNA copy number for men with metabolic syndromes increased when they consumed 3 g/day of KRG and the mean change in their mtDNA copy number was significantly higher than that of the group who consumed a placebo [19].

Third, the KRG group showed improvements in fatigue symptoms. A meta-analysis reported that red ginseng intake does not statistically significantly reduce fatigue symptoms [32]. Another randomized, placebo-controlled study did not show that KRG consumption resulted in a significant decrease in fatigue symptoms for the full sample, but a subgroup analysis showed that it did for people over 50 years old with moderate fatigue symptoms [33]. In this study, the KRG could reduce fatigue symptoms in postmenopausal women as confirmed with statical significance after the intervention.

On the other hand, the mean LDL cholesterol levels in the KRG group decreased from 136 to 127 mg/dL, but they did not decrease in the placebo group. However, this decrease was not statistically significant (p = 0.067). A previous study showed that administering 6 g/day of P. ginseng extract for 8 weeks decreased LDL cholesterol in males [34]. Another clinical study with hyperlipidemic patients reported that LDL cholesterol decreased significantly in the red ginseng (2 g/day) and placebo group, but there was no significant difference between the two groups [35]. The subjects of that study were young, male, and hyperlipidemic, while this study was conducted on postmenopausal women. Therefore, this difference seems to indicate a dissimilarity in the study results. However, even though the baseline LDL cholesterol level was in the normal range, it showed a tendency to decrease after the intervention in postmenopausal women. A large sample and long-term clinical study are necessary to evaluate the effect of KRG on lipid metabolism in the future.

observations.literal_anchor:
This study is the first randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to investigate the comprehensive efficacy of KRG administration on biological aging, antioxidant activity, and clinical symptoms in Korean postmenopausal women. However, this study also has some limitations. The first limitation is that the KRG group was administered 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks. Previous clinical studies that evaluated changes in mtDNA copy number, antioxidant indicators, and clinical symptoms varied the dose of KRG from 1 to 6 g/day and the duration of administration from 2 to 12 weeks. These ranges indicate that the dose and duration of KRG administration are not strongly agreed upon, so use of higher doses or longer administration durations in this study may have produced different outcomes, including LDL cholesterol. However, a daily dose of 2 g of KRG is generally available as a healthy functional supplement in the market. Accordingly, in this study, we selected 2 g per day, the dosage for safety KRG intake as a general health functional food. Therefore, determining the optimal dose and duration for KRG intervention should be further investigated in the future. The second limitation is that, although we told the participants to keep their usual lifestyle during the clinical trial, we could not strictly control each individual’s behaviors, which could affect biological aging, antioxidant capacity, and clinical symptoms. The third limitation is that the participants were all Korean postmenopausal women, so the results may not be broadly generalizable to other populations, such as men, premenopausal women, and different ethnicities.

TITLE
5. Conclusions

P
This study examined the effects of KRG consumption on the primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms, in Korean postmenopausal women. The results showed that administering 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks increased the mtDNA copy number, increased antioxidant activity, and reduced fatigue symptoms more than the placebo.

Six participants were excluded from the placebo group, 1 of whom had abdominal pain, 2 of whom had constipation, 1 of whom took multivitamin supplements, and 2 of whom took other red ginseng products. A total of 33 participants in the KRG group and 30 participants in the placebo group completed the study. Figure 1 shows a flow chart for how the study was conducted.

Figure 1
Flowchart of the study.

TITLE
2.2. Randomization

P
Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily. Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code. These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute, Inc., Cary, NC, USA). Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

TITLE
2.3. Korean Red Ginseng and Placebo Supplements

P
Participants in the KRG group received 2 g of KRG tablet per day. The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd. The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet). The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets. The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

4. Discussion

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Population/design/registration
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Study examination dates
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: between August 2019 and March 2021

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Inclusion and exclusion population
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Randomized allocation denominator
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Active attrition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: 4 participants from the KRG group were excluded

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Placebo attrition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Six participants were excluded from the placebo group

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Dose route frequency
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Sequence allocation wording
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Allocation software
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Blinding
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Composition
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Extract preparation
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Placebo matrix
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Intervention supplier
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: FSS item format
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: FSS printed summed range
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical rationale
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: We analyzed the data based on the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem because each group had at least 30 participants.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical between contrast
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The mean differences in changes between the groups were compared using independent two-sample t-tests.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Statistical threshold
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: All statistical tests were two-sided and p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Blood extraction
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: All DNA samples were extracted from ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-treated blood.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: mtDNA formula
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Ct18S–CtND5, where the mean amount of mtDNA = 2−ΔCt

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Outcome hierarchy
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Funding
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: This study was supported by a 2018 research grant from the Korean Society of Ginseng (GS 305-354).

parent_all47_literal_anchors.label: Conflict declaration
parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

parent_all47_literal_anchors.literal: Not applicable.

flags.source_bound_issue: KRG tablet dehydrated from extract; no full botanical extraction recipe, extraction solvent, specific manufacturer/brand/lot or independent purity certificate provided.
flags.consequence: Preparation-specific evidence; generic retail KRG, raw ginseng and isolates equivalence UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The eight listed concentrations describe a mixture. Actual adherence, exposure/PK, and isolated ingredient contributions were not measured.
flags.consequence: Empty ingredient aliases; conditional nominal doses are not efficacy or exposure evidence.

flags.source_bound_issue: Cornstarch/cellulose and same flavor described; quantities, visual/texture matching and blinding success assessment not reported.
flags.consequence: Reported double blinding retained; verified masking success UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Source says SAS-generated codes and sequential alternating assignment by code; method of sequence generation, allocation concealment and implementation details insufficient to reconstruct.
flags.consequence: Retain source RCT claim with unclear allocation wording; neither assured concealment nor definite nonrandom assignment inferred.

flags.source_bound_issue: The main article names SAS 9.4 for allocation, whereas the registry names SAS 9.2.
flags.consequence: Printed conflict retained; original actual software/version UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The article reports 73 randomized (37/36) and 63 completed (33/30). Active losses: two unknown reasons in text versus two lost contact in the native flowchart, one surgery admission, one multivitamin use. Placebo losses: one abdominal pain, two constipation, one multivitamin use, two other-ginseng use.
flags.consequence: Completer analysis rather than claimed ITT; reasons do not establish causality.

flags.source_bound_issue: Endpoint-specific n, imputation, missing-not-at-random sensitivity and ITT estimates not provided.
flags.consequence: Selection by completion may bias estimates; do not assume complete63 for every molecular assay.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry target is 80 (40 per arm); its Final Enrollment Number field is 63, whereas the article reports 73 randomized and 63 analyzed completers.
flags.consequence: Preserve labels; actual target enrollment is not analyzed denominator, registry63 not proof only63 randomized.

flags.source_bound_issue: CRIS first submission is 2021-08-12 and registration is 2021-08-26, after study completion on 2021-03-20; WHO explicitly marks Prospective Registration No.
flags.consequence: Current registration cannot establish outcome prespecification before recruitment or analysis.

flags.source_bound_issue: Article examination dates are August 2019–March 2021. Registry first enrollment is 2019-10-04, primary completion 2020-06-26, study completion 2021-03-20.
flags.consequence: Different date meanings retained; do not infer exact participant overlap or undocumented amendment.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry primary outcomes include DNA telomere length and total oxidative status in addition to mtDNA/TAS. The extra two primary outcomes are not reported in this main article.
flags.consequence: Reporting-completeness concern; no outcome-failure or deliberate selectivity inference.

flags.source_bound_issue: Registry planned assessments include BUN, creatinine, urine analysis, body composition, and menopause rating scale in the lay summary. The main reports FSS and limited metabolic labs; these extra outcomes are not reported.
flags.consequence: Missing outcome reporting remains UNKNOWN, not null renal/muscle/menopause results.

flags.source_bound_issue: The protocol field is labeled flow chart.pdf. The results field is labeled Table_Results.pdf, but both WHO-linked and direct endpoints delivered identical two-page flowchart bytes (SHA2564622991b...). No genuine methods protocol, SAP or results-table attachment was obtained.
flags.consequence: One complete flow attachment read; zero complete protocol/SAP/results-table attachment credit.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is explicitly secondary; biomarkers are primary. No prospectively bound fatigue threshold or primary strength endpoint is available.
flags.consequence: Narrow subjective-fatigue qualification only; not definitive primary clinical function efficacy.

flags.source_bound_issue: Tests use unadjusted two-sided P<.05 across metabolic variables, mtDNA change/fold, TAS and FSS. No multiplicity correction, prespecified SAP or confirmatory hierarchy is provided.
flags.consequence: Reported P retained; falsepositive/selectivity uncertainty, not automatic corrected significant result.

flags.source_bound_issue: The article cites the CLT/law of large numbers with at least 30 participants per group, but gives no effect-based power/sample-size calculation or comparative CIs.
flags.consequence: Nonsignificance not equivalence; distribution assumptions and clinical precision UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Baseline leukocytes are 4890±931 versus 5553±1361 (P=.027), and total cholesterol 230±31 versus 210±41 (P=.034). No baseline-adjusted outcome model is reported.
flags.consequence: Potential confounding/precision and blood-cell composition concern; no proven cause of outcome.

flags.source_bound_issue: Usual lifestyle was encouraged, but authors acknowledge it was not strictly controlled. Baseline physical activity is 17/33 versus 10/30 (P=.145).
flags.consequence: No randomized exercise effect; nonsignificant baseline differences do not prove equality.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS has nine items scored 1–7; the printed summed range is 7–63. The conditional arithmetic minimum is 9 if all nine items score 1.
flags.consequence: Retain7–63literal; conditional arithmetic audit not correction of questionnaire scoring.

flags.source_bound_issue: FSS is self-report. The discussion calls fatigue objectively evaluated using a validated questionnaire, but no objective strength or task test was performed.
flags.consequence: Self-report instrument, not force/performance/strength gain.

flags.source_bound_issue: Exact Korean version, validation in this population, recall window, missing-item rule, MCID and responder threshold are not supplied. No fatigue severity entry criterion is stated.
flags.consequence: Clinical importance and applicability to symptomatic chronic fatigue UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Reported visits are baseline and eight weeks only. Long-term follow-up and post-withdrawal durability are not reported.
flags.consequence: Do not extrapolate long-term efficacy/safety.

flags.source_bound_issue: Relative blood mtDNA qPCR and TAS are proxies. Mitochondrial respiration, ATP, muscle bioenergetics, pathway activation and clinical aging endpoints were not measured.
flags.consequence: No proved aging reversal or muscle mitochondrial rescue.

flags.source_bound_issue: Introduction calls the measure lymphocyte mtDNA; methods describe DNA from EDTA peripheral blood without lymphocyte isolation or subtype adjustment.
flags.consequence: Cell composition influence and exact lymphocyte specificity UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: The printed formula defines ΔCt=Ct18S−CtND5 and quantity=2^−ΔCt. Under the usual equal-efficiency ND5/18S normalization this appears to reverse the sign convention.
flags.consequence: Retain printed equation; conditional algebra only, rawCt/calculationverification unavailable.

flags.source_bound_issue: Table1 KRG baseline mtDNA is 4.35±2.54, while Table3/body gives 4.36±2.54.
flags.consequence: Retain both; do not silently normalize rounding.

flags.source_bound_issue: Native Figure2B labels eight-week KRG mtDNA 5.98; Table3/body prints 5.93.
flags.consequence: No plot/table source equivalence assumption; retain5.98and5.93.

flags.source_bound_issue: Table2 KRG gamma-GT means are 17→19 U/L, while reported change is −2±7; arithmetic from those means would give +2.
flags.consequence: Retain printednegativechangeandnullP=.243; conditional arithmetic not data repair.

flags.source_bound_issue: KRG baseline DBP is 73.0±11.6 in Table1 versus 73.3±11.6 in Table2. Placebo baseline SD is 7.9 in Table1 versus 9.6 in Table2. Table2 KRG change is 1.4 despite printed means 74.4−73.3=1.1.
flags.consequence: Printed conflicts/rounded-summary limits retained; no automatic correction.

flags.source_bound_issue: All 12 Table2 comparative P values are at least .05, including LDL .064 and AST .082. No metabolic within-group change is reported as significant.
flags.consequence: Preserve nulls; trends do not become positive efficacy or universal absence.

flags.source_bound_issue: No participant-level association/mediation analysis linking FSS to biomarkers, or pathway experiment, is reported.
flags.consequence: TAS/mtDNA cochanges do not prove fatigue mechanism.

flags.source_bound_issue: Placebo gastrointestinal withdrawals and active surgery/lost-contact cases are described. There is no systematic AE grade/frequency table, causality/severity assessment, or complete serious-event follow-up.
flags.consequence: Formal AE/SAEtotal UNKNOWN, not zero; placeboevents do not prove KRG harmless.

flags.source_bound_issue: Kidney disease was excluded. The registry planned creatinine/BUN, but these results are not reported in the article.
flags.consequence: No renal safety conclusion, no extension to renal disease or general drug interactions.

flags.source_bound_issue: Population is Korean postmenopausal women aged 46–69 without movement restrictions, not an MVA/BUB1B cohort. No objective strength test was reported.
flags.consequence: No population/formulation pooling, sex extrapolation or BUB1B/MVA rescue.

flags.source_bound_issue: The Korean Society of Ginseng funded the study (2018, GS305-354) and supplied tablets. Registry project ID is 2174-2498 and sponsor is Yonsei/Gangnam Severance Hospital. Authors declare no conflicts.
flags.consequence: Funding/supply context preserved; project identity/independent product provenance UNKNOWN.

flags.source_bound_issue: Article data availability is Not applicable; registry IPD sharing is No.
flags.consequence: No rawdata/patient-level reanalysis or exposure confirmation.

flags.source_bound_issue: Current EPMC has no commentCorrectionList and hasSuppl N; XML has no related-article or supplementary-material nodes. Main HTML and Notes return403; browser Notes returns429. Bounded searches retrieved no exact new notice body.
flags.consequence: No current publisher-equivalence or exhaustive no-notice claim; zero notice bodies read.

flags.source_bound_issue: History listing shows one 2021-08-12 row. No separate historical version-detail body was opened.
flags.consequence: No prospective historical plan/amendment equivalence claim.

exact_source.title: The Effects of Korean Red Ginseng on Biological Aging and Antioxidant Capacity in Postmenopausal Women: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Study

parent_original_qualification.functional_basis: Actual assigned oral preparation versus concurrent placebo, with measured secondary FSS self-report fatigue and reported between-group change contrast. No objective strength/task measure.

preparation.placebo: Cornstarch/cellulose tablets with same flavor; quantities unknown

allocation.analysis: Appears to use completers; ITT and imputation not reported

allocation.shared_lifestyle: Usual lifestyle encouraged but not strictly controlled; no randomized exercise

TITLE
4. Discussion

original_parent_anchor.label: Population/design/registration
original_parent_anchor.literal: This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial.

original_parent_anchor.label: Study examination dates
original_parent_anchor.literal: between August 2019 and March 2021

original_parent_anchor.label: Inclusion and exclusion population
original_parent_anchor.literal: Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years

original_parent_anchor.label: Randomized allocation denominator
original_parent_anchor.literal: A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.

original_parent_anchor.label: Active attrition
original_parent_anchor.literal: 4 participants from the KRG group were excluded

original_parent_anchor.label: Placebo attrition
original_parent_anchor.literal: Six participants were excluded from the placebo group

original_parent_anchor.label: Dose route frequency
original_parent_anchor.literal: Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily.

original_parent_anchor.label: Sequence allocation wording
original_parent_anchor.literal: Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code.

original_parent_anchor.label: Allocation software
original_parent_anchor.literal: These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4

original_parent_anchor.label: Blinding
original_parent_anchor.literal: Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

original_parent_anchor.label: Composition
original_parent_anchor.literal: The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd.

original_parent_anchor.label: Extract preparation
original_parent_anchor.literal: The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet).

original_parent_anchor.label: Placebo matrix
original_parent_anchor.literal: The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets.

original_parent_anchor.label: Intervention supplier
original_parent_anchor.literal: The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

original_parent_anchor.label: FSS item format
original_parent_anchor.literal: It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points.

original_parent_anchor.label: FSS printed summed range
original_parent_anchor.literal: Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical rationale
original_parent_anchor.literal: We analyzed the data based on the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem because each group had at least 30 participants.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical between contrast
original_parent_anchor.literal: The mean differences in changes between the groups were compared using independent two-sample t-tests.

original_parent_anchor.label: Statistical threshold
original_parent_anchor.literal: All statistical tests were two-sided and p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

original_parent_anchor.label: Blood extraction
original_parent_anchor.literal: All DNA samples were extracted from ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-treated blood.

original_parent_anchor.label: mtDNA formula
original_parent_anchor.literal: Ct18S–CtND5, where the mean amount of mtDNA = 2−ΔCt

original_parent_anchor.label: Outcome hierarchy
original_parent_anchor.literal: primary outcomes for variables of interest, which were changes in biological aging marker and antioxidant capacity, and secondary variables of interest, which were fatigue symptoms

original_parent_anchor.label: Funding
original_parent_anchor.literal: This study was supported by a 2018 research grant from the Korean Society of Ginseng (GS 305-354).

original_parent_anchor.label: Conflict declaration
original_parent_anchor.literal: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

original_parent_anchor.label: Data availability
original_parent_anchor.literal: Not applicable.

TITLE
4. Discussion

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: KRG tablet dehydrated from extract; no full botanical extraction recipe, extraction solvent, specific manufacturer/brand/lot or independent purity certificate provided.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Preparation-specific evidence; generic retail KRG, raw ginseng and isolates equivalence UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The eight listed concentrations describe a mixture. Actual adherence, exposure/PK, and isolated ingredient contributions were not measured.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Empty ingredient aliases; conditional nominal doses are not efficacy or exposure evidence.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Cornstarch/cellulose and same flavor described; quantities, visual/texture matching and blinding success assessment not reported.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Reported double blinding retained; verified masking success UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: Source says SAS-generated codes and sequential alternating assignment by code; method of sequence generation, allocation concealment and implementation details insufficient to reconstruct.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Retain source RCT claim with unclear allocation wording; neither assured concealment nor definite nonrandom assignment inferred.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The main article names SAS 9.4 for allocation, whereas the registry names SAS 9.2.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Printed conflict retained; original actual software/version UNKNOWN.

all38_original_parent_flags.source_bound_issue: The article reports 73 randomized (37/36) and 63 completed (33/30). Active losses: two unknown reasons in text versus two lost contact in the native flowchart, one surgery admission, one multivitamin use. Placebo losses: one abdominal pain, two constipation, one multivitamin use, two other-ginseng use.
all38_original_parent_flags.consequence: Completer analysis rather than claimed ITT; reasons do not establish causality.

admitted_ledger_entry.rationale: One reported double-blind placebo-controlled study in Korean postmenopausal women aged 46–69 compares four 500 mg extract-derived tablets daily (2 g/day) for eight weeks with flavor-matched cornstarch/cellulose placebo. Of 73 randomized (37/36), 63 completed (33/30). Secondary FSS total changed −7±12 versus −1±11, P=.033; baseline/end totals 34±16→27±14 versus 32±15→31±16. The named patient-reported total retains a narrow fatigue comparison, with unknown exact version/item implementation, CI, clinical importance and isolated physical-subdomain effect. Objective force/task performance was unmeasured. TAS change .11±.25 versus −.04±.16 mmol/L, P=.011; blood mtDNA change 1.58±2.05 versus .28±2.36, P=.023, and fold change 1.44±.46 versus 1.15±.40, P=.012 remain biomarkers, without clinical rejuvenation or muscle-mitochondrial/BUB1B inference. All 12 displayed metabolic change comparisons are nonpositive; no equivalence is established. Sequential alternating-code wording, SAS-version discrepancy, baseline differences, completer analysis and missing outcome/harms data limit causal certainty. Registration was after completion and planned telomere, total oxidative status and other clinical/renal/urine/body-composition measures lack displayed results; multiplicity and original hierarchy remain unresolved. Printed FSS range, mtDNA formula/table/figure, DBP and gamma-GT conflicts remain unchanged. Placebo abdominal pain/constipation, active surgery/hospitalization, lost contact and other losses are retained without assigning cause; complete AE ascertainment and broad safety remain unknown. Author discussion of prior fatigue nulls/subgroups and animal/in-vitro mechanisms is reference context, not independently reviewed synthesis. This source-specific whole preparation does not establish generic ginseng, isolated ginsenoside efficacy, BUB1B/MVA rescue or superiority to niacin, NMN, apitegromab or qualified creatine populations. Nominees remain unchanged.
admitted_ledger_entry.identity_limit: Only the tested extract-derived Korean red ginseng tablets, supplied by Korean Society of Ginseng, are qualified. Manufacturer, brand, batch, purity, constituent-basis certainty and retail equivalence remain unknown. Placebo ingredient quantities are unknown. Empty aliases prevent generic ginseng, Panax, isolated ginsenosides or commercial product inheritance. Adds one source-specific appraisal, no new chemical, accepted eligibility screen or verified independent trial family.

observations.literal_anchor:
There were 63 participants, of whom 33 received KRG and 30 received a placebo. The mtDNA copy number (KRG group: 1.58 ± 2.05, placebo group: 0.28 ± 2.36, p = 0.023) and TAS (KRG group: 0.11 ± 0.25 mmol/L, placebo group: −0.04 ± 0.16 mmol/L, p = 0.011) increased and the fatigue severity scale (KRG group: −7 ± 12, placebo group: −1 ± 11, p = 0.033) decreased significantly more in the KRG group than the placebo group. KRG significantly increased the mtDNA copy number, total antioxidant status, and improved symptoms of fatigue in postmenopausal women.Keywords: Korean red ginseng, antioxidant activity, biological aging, fatigue, postmenopausal women

observations.literal_anchor:
2.1. Study Design and Participants

P
This study comprised an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial. Participants were examined at the Severance Health Check-up, Severance Hospital, Yonsei University Health System, in Seoul, Korea, between August 2019 and March 2021. This study’s protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Gangnam Severance Hospital (IRB no.: 3-2019-0089) and registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS, KCT0006506). This study was performed in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

P
Eligible participants were postmenopausal women aged 46–69 years who could communicate in Korean naturally and who were not participating in any other interventional studies. Additionally, participants had to have no physical restrictions on movement. Those who were excluded were current smokers; those who consumed more than 3 standard alcoholic drinks more than two days per week; who had uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥ 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) ≥ 100 mmHg; who had uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, defined as having fasting plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL; who had been diagnosed with liver disease and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels more than three times the upper limit; who had been diagnosed with kidney, cardiovascular, or cerebral vascular disease; who had any form of cancer or were undergoing cancer treatment; or who were taking other health supplements or female hormones. Written informed consent was obtained from all patients before participation.

P
A total of 73 participants were enrolled in this study, 37 of whom were randomly placed in the KRG group and 36 of whom were randomly placed in the placebo group.
observations.root_source_first_judgment: Population is Korean postmenopausal women aged 46–69 with free physical movement; exclusions constrain transfer to disease/frailty/BUB1B populations. Recruitment is reported August2019–March2021 in main, whereas registry first enrollment is October2019. Preserve both.

observations.literal_anchor:
2.2. Randomization

P
Participants were randomly assigned to take a 500 mg KRG or placebo tablet four times daily. Participants were assigned to each group in an even ratio by sequentially assigning them in alternating order by their assignment code. These codes were generated using SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute, Inc., Cary, NC, USA). Both researchers and participants were blinded to the assignments throughout the study.

TITLE
2.3. Korean Red Ginseng and Placebo Supplements

P
Participants in the KRG group received 2 g of KRG tablet per day. The tablets contained 8.03 mg/g of ginsenoside Rb1, 3.29 mg/g of Rc, 2.80 mg/g of Rb2, 2.50 mg/g of Rg3, 1.47 mg/g of Rf, 1.29 mg/g of Re, 1.18 mg/g of Rg1, and 1.0 mg/g of Rd. The KRG tablets were prepared by dehydrating KRG extract (3 g of KRG extract per 2 g tablet). The placebo tablets contained cornstarch and cellulose with the same flavor as the KRG tablets. The KRG and placebo tablet were provided by the study sponsor (The Korean Society of Ginseng, Seoul, Korea).

TITLE
2.4. Data Collection

P
Each participant completed a questionnaire about lifestyle, medical history, and health supplements. Self-reported cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, and physical activity were extracted from the questionnaires. Current alcohol consumption was defined as drinking less than 2 cups of alcoholic beverages a day per week. Participants were asked about their physical exercise on a weekly basis, and physical activity was defined as exercising more than 3 times per week with moderate-to-vigorous intensity. P
TAS was measured using a TBA c8000 automated colorimeter (Toshiba Medical system Ltd., Tokyo, Japan). The antioxidative molecules in the sample reduce dark blue-green-colored 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzo-thiazoline-6-sulfonate) radicals into a colorless form according to antioxidant concentrations and capacities. The change in absorbance at 660 nm is related to the total amount of antioxidants in the sample. The TAS assay was calibrated with Trolox equivalent, a stable, standard antioxidant solution and a vitamin E analog [12].

TITLE
2.5.3. Fatigue Severity Scale

P
The FSS is a popular tool for measuring fatigue symptoms [13]. It has been validated for various diseases, such as multiple sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosis, Parkinson’s disease, and stroke [14,15,16]. It consists of 9 items, each of which can receive a score of 1–7 points. Fatigue severity is the sum of each item’s score for a total score range of 7–63 where higher scores indicate more severe fatigue symptoms.

TITLE
4. Discussion

P
This study comprised a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the effect of KRG consumption on biological aging, antioxidant capacity, and fatigue symptoms in postmenopausal women. We found that taking 2 g/day of KRG for 8 weeks increased mtDNA copy number and TAS and reduced fatigue symptoms more than the placebo. Our findings are consistent with those of previous studies on the effectiveness of KRG.

P
First, in this study, KRG was shown to increase the mtDNA copy number more than the placebo. A previous study showed that KRG improved exercise performance, increased the ATP production capacity of muscle cells, and stimulated myoblast differentiation in mice [17]. An animal study showed that the mtDNA copy number and messenger RNA expression levels of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors increased more in those with diabetes who took KRG than those who took a placebo [18]. A clinical trial showed that the mtDNA copy number for men with metabolic syndromes increased when they consumed 3 g/day of KRG and the mean change in their mtDNA copy number was significantly higher than that of the group who consumed a placebo [19].
